To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C-terminal SH2 domain of CAP binds to a conserved motif, PXPPXRPXSSL, in the Cbl protein.
we have identified a peptide sequence that is a high affinity ligand for the SH3 domain of the CAP protein.
the C-terminal SH 3 domain of CAP binds to the SH3 ligand motifs of Cbl and Sos with high affinity and specificity, and that this interaction is mediated by a common consensus motif, PXPPXRYXSSL.
In summary, our research is concerned with

identifying and characterizing the molecular recognition properties of a novel SH3 domain, which may be a key component in a signal transduction pathway that regulates cell adhesion and cell motility.

the identification of ligands for the C-terminal Sh 3 domain of the novel cytoskeletal adaptor protein CAP, which may be involved in the assembly of signal transduction complexes at the cell membrane.
the identification of ligand sites for one of the three SH3 domains in a cytoskeletal protein CAP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C-terminal SH 3 domain of CAP has the ability to interact with the c-Cbl and Son-of-sevenless proteins.
this SH3 domain of the CAP binds to the C-terminal region of c-Cbl, a protein that regulates tyrosine kinase signaling pathways.
the C-terminal SH 3 domain of CAP recognizes the consensus sequence, PXPPX RXSSL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal SH2 domain of CAP recognizes the Cbl SH3 domain, which in turn recognizes the SH2 domain of the C-terminal SHC domain.
the C-terminal SH 3 domain of CAP recognizes the consensus sequence PXPPXRXSXL.
the C-terminal SH-3 domain of CAP recognizes the consensus sequence, PXPPXRPXSSL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal SH 3 domain of CAP has a unique binding specificity for peptide ligands, and that the binding site is located in a 16 amino acid segment of the c-Cub protein.
